turns.content: A barley gene encodes an enzyme that produces an anti-nutritional compound. Using the intact coding-strand prefix 5'-ATGTTTCTCGCTGGTACTTCTGTGGATGAACATATTTATTGTCGT...TGA-3', set the reading frame from ATG and translate the first six codons.
Describe how you would compare each mutant coding prefix with the intact sequence to identify synonymous, in-frame, and premature-stop changes that could disrupt enzyme production.

In the shared 5'-to-3' reading frame, compare Mutant 1, 5'-ATGTTCTACGCTGGTACTTCTGTGGATGAACATATTTATTGTCGC...TGA-3', and Mutant 2, 5'-ATGTTCTAAGCTGGTACTTCTGTGGATGAACATATTTATTGTCGC...TGA-3', with the intact prefix.
Focus on Mutant 2 prefix ATGTTCTAAGCTGGT. Identify its earliest translated consequence in the shared frame.

Compare Mutant 3, 5'-ATGTTTTACGCTGGTGTCACTTCTGTGGATGAACATATTTATTGTCGT...TGA-3', and Mutant 4, 5'-ATGTTTTACGCTACTTCTGTGGATGAACATATTTATTGTCGT...TGA-3', with the intact sequence. Classify their early coding changes and check for a premature stop.
Which mutant is most likely to abolish production of the anti-nutritional compound, and what molecular consequence makes it the strongest loss-of-function candidate?
Translate the selected mutant through its first termination codon and contrast that early truncation with the in-frame insertion or deletion in the other mutants.
Discuss the likely effects on translation and nonsense-mediated decay, and name the protein, enzyme-activity, or metabolite measurements needed to confirm loss of pathway output.
State the selected mutant and explain why its early coding consequence is more decisive than the synonymous or in-frame changes in the other lines.
